title: Allocation-context and reclaim side effects
summary: Source-backed research candidate for a recurring semantic dependency. No active KOLVRT consumer, compatibility implementation or measured cost is claimed.

history.linux_behavior: GFP_KERNEL permits sleeping and direct reclaim. GFP_NOFS/GFP_NOIO historically avoid filesystem or I/O recursion; scoped APIs are preferred since 4.12.
history.historical_reason: Reclaim recovers memory under pressure while context restrictions prevent recursive deadlocks and distinguish reserve access.
history.root_cause: Allocation policy carries execution-context and subsystem side effects that a legacy consumer may depend on.
history.unknown_origin_reason: The pinned documentation establishes the described behavior, not its first introducing release/commit. Historical origin requires separate investigation.

native.behavior: Current IRQ paths neither allocate nor take heap/table locks. A future EL0 allocation contract must explicitly define reclaim and failure; no general allocation service is implemented.
native.why_differs: A Linux-facing adapter cannot silently introduce reclaim work into native IRQ execution. Which EL0 semantics actually need translation remains unverified.
